text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet raised petrol prices by some 10 percent, and diesel prices by around nine percent, effective from Friday, because of the sharp fall of the lev against the dollar in the past two weeks. @

-- Bulgaria's president Zhelyu Zhelev said the currency board system proposed by the International Monetary Fund to enforce strict monetary control in Bulgaria was the last chance to rescue the country's democracy.

-- Fake dollar and mark notes had flooded Bulgaria's Black Sea port of Varna in the last two weeks as Bulgarians rushed to exchange levs for foreign currency because of the sharp fall in the lev, police said.
-- Bulgaria's Health Ministry said it had registered 185 HIV positive Bulgarians for the last 10 years and 43 of them died of AIDS. @
-- Bulgaria's Foreign Investment Agency director Daniela Bobeva said she had resigned, because she failed to prevent introduction of new legislative barriers for foreign investors.
-- Bulgaria plans to offer for sale next year up to 49 percent of the state cigarete maker Bulgartabak holding, as a part of its privatisation programme, Trade Minister Atanas Paparisov said.
-- Bulgaria's central bank (BNB) said it cancelled licences of another three financial houses and three exchange bureaus due to violations of BNB forex trade regulations. @
-- Bulgaria is expected to call a grain import tender for 300,000 tonnes of wheat among seven leading grain trading companies, Trade Minister Atanas Paparisov said.
-- Bulgaria's state Biochim bank signed a technical cooperation agreement with the Dutch ABN AMRO bank, a Biochim senior official said.

-- Russia is expected to extend $400 million credit to Bulgaria for the upgrade of Bulgaria's Kozlodui nuclear power plant as $250 million will be used for the upgrade of the four small reactors and the other $150 will secure Russia's participation in an international consortium to modernize the other two reactors, Bulgaria's Energy minister Roumen Ovcharov said.

-- Unidentified gunmen killed and robbed the cashier of the Bulgarian Fisk brokerage house in the stairway of a building in central Sofia as he left Fisk's office carrying a large amount of foreign currency in cash, police officials said. @
